pitch_detail.notes: Broad gully; stay center/right for the easiest class-2 line
The gully tops out around 8,150 ft; the 8,514 ft summit is roughly 360 ft above

set.beta: From the Eightmile Trail, cut cross-country up through an old burn zone, then continue up and left toward the gully between the S and SE ridges. The S/SE gully is wide and offers a 'choose your own adventure' character: the center/right line is mostly class 2, while the climbers-left side holds solid class 3-4 rock. The gully tops out at roughly 8,150 ft, about 360 vertical feet below the 8,514 ft summit. This line cuts the standard 8-9 mile one-way West Ridge approach roughly in half.

findings.evidence: No source gives section lengths for the gully; the 111 m total (= length_m) is also far short of a gully that tops out ~360 ft below an 8,514 ft summit after a long cross-country climb. Dropped both lengthM keys; nothing else changed.

findings.claim: IDENTITY: is the East Ledges a climbable ascent route or only a descent?
findings.evidence: Both. SummitPost has a dedicated East Ledges route page treating it as an ascent ('technically probably the easiest route to the summit', with a small-rack recommendation for ascending), while noting it is mostly unprotectable and usually used as the descent after the West Ridge / East Ridge Direct. So a separate row is defensible, but the row's own overview and approach call it 'not a recommended ascent line' reached 'only from the summit', framing it purely as a descent. Human decision whether to keep it as a route; if kept, that framing should be reconciled.
